record.paper_title: Boundary and Defect CFT: Open Problems and Applications
record.original_question: Can extended chiral or superconformal algebras be used systematically to construct new non-topological, non-factorizing conformal defects in tricritical Ising theory and related models?

evidence.quote: We would like to look further into the use of extended algebras to construct new conformal defects.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the two-dimensional tricritical Ising conformal field theory, i.e. the unitary Virasoro minimal model M(4,5) with central charge c = 7/10, as well as its supersymmetric (fermionic) version with N=1 superconformal symmetry, and more generally rational conformal field theories whose chiral algebra admits a non-trivial extension (for instance by a current of integer or half-integer spin, by a W-algebra, or by a superconformal algebra).

A conformal defect between two such CFTs is a one-dimensional interface that preserves the total stress tensor T - \bar T continuity across the defect, but is not required to commute separately with the holomorphic and antiholomorphic Virasoro algebras. A conformal defect is called:
- topological if T and \bar T are separately continuous across it (so that it commutes with the full Virasoro algebra and can be freely deformed);
- factorizing if it is a sum of products of a boundary state and a dual boundary state (i.e. it is equivalent to a pair of conformal boundary conditions);
- non-topological and non-factorizing otherwise.

A standard tool to construct conformal defects is the folding trick: a defect between CFTs C_1 and C_2 is identified with a conformal boundary condition of the tensor-product theory C_1 \otimes \bar C_2. Boundary conditions preserving an extended chiral algebra in the folded theory then yield defects in the unfolded theory.

Problem. Develop a systematic construction, based on extended chiral algebras (including W-algebras and N=1 or higher superconformal algebras) of the folded theory, that produces conformal defects in the tricritical Ising model (and in related rational CFTs such as other Virasoro minimal models and their supersymmetric or W-extended counterparts) which are simultaneously non-topological and non-factorizing. Specifically:

(a) Identify which extensions of the chiral algebra of the folded theory C \otimes \bar C, for C the tricritical Ising model, admit boundary conditions that descend, after unfolding, to defects that are provably neither topological nor factorizing.

(b) Classify the resulting conformal defects up to equivalence, compute their reflection and transmission coefficients, and determine the algebra they generate under fusion.

(c) Determine whether this extended-algebra construction generates genuinely new conformal defects beyond those obtainable from elementary topological and factorizing defects, and extend the construction to other minimal models and superconformal minimal models.
artifact.status_search_result: Partial progress exists: a construction of new conformal, non-topological, non-factorizing defects in the tricritical Ising minimal model has been carried out by exploiting the superconformal (fermionic) extension and the folding trick to a c=7/5 fermionic theory, producing defects beyond elementary topological/factorizing ones. However, a fully systematic theory using general extended chiral or W-algebras for tricritical Ising and related minimal/superconformal models is not established, and broader classification questions remain open.

status_evidence.title: Defects in the tri-critical Ising model
status_evidence.snippet: New conformal (but not topological or factorised) defects were constructed in the minimal model by first constructing defects in the fermionic model as boundary conditions in a fermionic theory of central charge c=7/5, using the folding trick.
status_evidence.claim: Some non-topological non-factorizing conformal defects in tricritical Ising are constructed via the superconformal extension and folding trick.

status_evidence.title: Duality defects in E8
status_evidence.snippet: There can be defects that commute with the Virasoro algebra but do not preserve the fully extended chiral algebra, illustrating defects not expressible in terms of elementary topological and factorised defects.
status_evidence.claim: Extended chiral algebras provide a route to defects beyond elementary topological/factorizing ones, but a systematic framework for tricritical Ising is not given.
